newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia C.Bank to tighten foreign bank requirements.
newsitem.headline: Russia C.Bank to tighten foreign bank requirements.

text.p: The Central Bank will tighten rules for foreign banks operating in Russia, First Deputy bank chairman Alexander Khandruyev said on Tuesday.

He said as of May 15 only foreign entities registered as banks in their home countries could open Russian subsidiaries, and subsidiaries' minimum charter capital requirement would rise to 10 million ecu from five million.
Khandruyev said premier foreign banks were good for the banking system.
"But at the same time reasonable support of domestic banking system also corresponds to the strategic interests of the Russian federation and the development of the banking system," he said.

Foreign companies need Central Bank permission to set up subsidiaries or purchase stakes in registered Russian banks. But acquisitions of less than one percent require will only require regional Central Bank branch permission under the new rule.
Foreigners' total share of the banking system remains capped at 12 percent, Khandruyev said.
Foreign capital accounts for 4.05 percent of Russian banking system capital but will rise to 6.8 percent if nine applications to set up subsidiaries being considered are approved, he said.
"Recently we have noticed that the biggest banks in Central and Eastern Europe have increased their efforts to open (Russian) subsidiaries," he said.
Russia has imposed curbs on foreign banks' operations until July 1999 to protect its domestic banking system.
Until then, foreign banks have only limited rights to deal in shares in Russian firms and may handle residents' accounts only of a minimum balance of 55,000 ecus.

Bank officials said existing foreign bank subsidiaries would have until January 1, 1998 to meet requirements top management include Russians or Russian-speakers, but said new charter capital requirements would apply only to new subsidiaries.
